pr_title: feat(hourglass): propose a research plan and gate retrieval on acceptance (#342)
title: Bind the fetch policy before passing the real fetch function
body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind the fetch policy before passing the real fetch function**

For an accepted plan naming an explicit URL, forwarding the plan here selects `web.gather_web_context`'s plan-execution branch, which ultimately calls `fetch_fn(url)` in `research_plan._fetch_source`. The supplied `_web.fetch_url` requires `allowed_hosts`, so every such fetch raises `TypeError: fetch_url() missing 1 required positional argument: 'allowed_hosts'` before making a request. The hourglass seam catches this and continues without the requested page's evidence. Bind the resolved allowlist and named-host policy into the fetch callable used by plan execution; the existing URL tests mock gathering and therefore miss this integration failure.

pr_title: feat(hourglass): propose a research plan and gate retrieval on acceptance (#342)
title: Keep the request binding unchanged when resolving a remembered site
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep the request binding unchanged when resolving a remembered site**

For a web-enabled follow-up such as “audit the same site as before,” `run_hourglass_request` proposes and approves a plan bound to the original `prompt`, then appends the remembered target to `web_prompt`. Passing that augmented text into the plan-aware gatherer makes `execute_plan` reject it with `request_hash`, so neither search nor fetch runs. The renderer also skips the remembered target because the original proposal contains only a search query, not that URL. Resolve the remembered target before drafting the plan while preserving the original request text for binding validation; otherwise the existing same-site follow-up path silently loses all retrieval.

pr_title: feat(chat): gate the conversation lane's retrieval on an accepted plan (#342)
title: Bind fetch policy arguments before executing chat plans
body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind fetch policy arguments before executing chat plans**

For an accepted chat request containing a URL, supplying `plan` switches `gather_web_context` to `execute_plan`, whose `_fetch_source` calls `fetch_fn(url)` without keyword arguments. However, `_gather_web_context` supplies the production `harness.web.fetch_url`, which requires `allowed_hosts`, so every such request raises `TypeError` before fetching anything and becomes a generic web-tools failure. The previous chat path supplied the allowlist and named-host policy. Bind those policy arguments into the fetch callable used by plan execution; the current tests hide this regression by replacing `fetch_url` with unrestricted mocks.

pr_title: feat(chat): gate the conversation lane's retrieval on an accepted plan (#342)
title: Propagate unknown provider usage instead of treating it as an outage
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Propagate unknown provider usage instead of treating it as an outage**

When plan evaluation raises `ProviderUsageUnknown`, this new broad handler converts it into an ordinary unavailable-review record with `cost: 0.0` and lets the request continue to answer generation. `JevPolicy.evaluate_research_plan` explicitly re-raises this exception because it carries known spend and unresolved billing liability; swallowing it discards those amounts and allows the hourglass lane, which previously propagated the exception, to continue spending and potentially finish successfully despite an unknown provider charge. Re-raise `ProviderUsageUnknown` alongside `ToolCancelled` rather than handling it as a recoverable reviewer outage.

pr_title: feat(hourglass): reuse a recorded plan acceptance on resume (#344)
title: Check receipt expiry when the caller omits now
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Check receipt expiry when the caller omits now**

When `decide_research_plan` receives `saved_plan` without an explicit `now`, it passes the default `None` into `validate_plan`, and `_approval_check` skips expiry enforcement when `now is None`. Consequently, an otherwise matching receipt with `expires_at=1` is returned as accepted with `reused=True`, without calling the reviewer. The hourglass caller supplies a timestamp, but the newly exposed helper API does not enforce this itself. Resolve the current time when `now` is omitted before validating a saved receipt so expired consent falls through to a fresh judgment.
